Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/backup

# Backup

Runs `~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1` right now. Same script the `com.keystone.dailybackup`
launchd agent runs at 21:00 daily (moved from 09:00 on 2026-09-24, when the Mac became the evening machine) — this is the on-demand path for when the Mac was shut at 21:00.

## Run it

Do not pre-check anything. Run first, report after.

```bash
/usr/bin/caffeinate -i /opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh -NoProfile -File ~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1 2>&1 | tail -40
```

Use a Bash `timeout` of `600000` (10 min). An awake run takes ~5-10 min, most of it the memsearch
INDEX step. Keep `caffeinate -i`: without it the Mac idle-sleeps on battery the moment the copies
finish, and INDEX crawls through brief dark wakes. On 2026-10-06 that turned a ~6 min index into
2 h. If a run outlasts the timeout, it moves to the background; wait for it, do not re-run.

## Read the verdict from state, not from the tail

```bash
cat ~/.claude/scripts/logs/backup-state.json
```

`status` is `OK` or `ERROR`; `errors` lists the failed job codes. That file is the authority.
The tail is for diagnosing, not for deciding.

**`status: OK` is not "everything was saved" — read `okCount` too.** A run that skipped the
SSD still ends `OK` with 0 errors. See the SSD gotcha below for what the count means.

## Then clear the stale hook error, if any

A failed run appends a line to `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log`, which is surfaced
as a HOOK FAILURE at every session start. A later successful run does **not** clear it. If `status`
is now `OK` and the file contains only `daily-backup:` lines, archive and empty it:

```bash
cp ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log.archived-$(date +%Y-%m-%d)
cp /dev/null ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log
```

If any non-`daily-backup` line is present, leave the file alone and tell the user what else is in it.
Shell truncation (`: > file`) under `$HOME` is blocked by dcg rule
`core.filesystem:redirect-truncate-root-home`, and there is no `truncate` binary here — use `cp /dev/null`.

## Report

Three lines, plain: did it work, what was skipped, what to do next. Never report "backup complete"
without naming a skipped target — a silent partial backup is the failure this skill exists to prevent.

## Gotchas

**Safe to ignore — expected on a healthy run:**
- `SNAP skip (missing): ~/.codex/memories` — that path has never existed.
- `TARGET baylor deprecated in manifest - snapshots to it SKIPPED` — deliberate.

**Real gaps — always surface these to the user:**
- `TARGET SSD /Volumes/CRASHBOX/AssistantBackup NOT MOUNTED - orphan and working-tree capture SKIPPED`
  — the run still reports `OK` with 0 errors, but **untracked, gitignored, and uncommitted-modified
  files were not saved anywhere.** GitHub and Google Drive cover only committed and pushed work.
  Tell the user to plug in CRASHBOX and run again. This is the most likely way to lose real work.

  **Cross-check with `okCount`, because the error count cannot see this.** `okCount` in
  `backup-state.json` is the number of jobs that ran, and two whole job classes — `CAPTURE`
  (per-project working-tree files) and `STATE-SSD` — exist only when the SSD is mounted. So:
  - **~31 jobs** = SSD captured. **~9-10 jobs** = SSD was absent; only the 4 `REPO` pushes and
    6 Drive `SNAP`s ran (verified against runs on 2026-09-04 and 2026-09-05).
  - A single-digit `okCount` with `status: OK` is the silent partial backup. Say so out loud.
  - Do not derive this from the error count or the exit code — both read `OK` either way.
- `TARGET ... NOT MOUNTED - is Google Drive for Desktop running?` — the Drive app is not running.
  Start it, then re-run.
- `PUSH ERR ... Could not resolve host: github.com` — a network blip, not a repo problem. Confirm
  with `ping -c1 github.com`, then just re-run; the commits are already made locally and will push.
  (Seen 2026-09-04 09:05: both `global-memory` and `skills` failed this way and a re-run fixed both.)
- `repo-diverged:<name>` — automation will never merge. Reconcile that repo by hand. For
  `dotclaude` and `global-memory` this almost always means the other machine pushed; `/dev-sync`
  Step 1 merges and pushes both (seen 2026-09-15).
- `STATE-SSD .codex : FAILED` with `rsync: error: skills/<name>: unlinkat: Directory not empty`
  just above it in `daily-backup.log` (the error only reaches the log file, not stdout). Cause:
  `sync-to-codex.sh` turned `~/.codex/skills/<name>` into a symlink, but the SSD copy is still a
  real folder. The copy is additive (no `--delete`, no `--force`), so rsync cannot swap a
  non-empty folder for a link — and it reports only some names per run, so fixing one reveals the
  next. List them all at once:
  `cd ~/.codex/skills && for e in *; do [ -L "$e" ] && [ -d "/Volumes/CRASHBOX/AssistantBackup/codex/skills/$e" ] && [ ! -L "/Volumes/CRASHBOX/AssistantBackup/codex/skills/$e" ] && echo "$e"; done`
  Move each one (literal paths — dcg blocks `mv` with `$VAR` paths) into
  `/Volumes/CRASHBOX/AssistantBackup/_OLD_codex-skills-dirs-<date>/`, then re-run. Never `rm`:
  the skills also live in the `claude-skills` repo, but the move is free. (Seen 2026-09-15:
  `dev-sync`, `new-project`, `startup`, `closeout`.)

**Other:**
- A nightly INDEX that takes hours (`INDEX path set` to `INDEX full set` in `daily-backup.log`) is the
  Mac asleep, not memsearch. With the lid closed at 21:00, launchd's `caffeinate -i -s` cannot keep it
  awake, so INDEX runs only in short dark wakes (`pmset -g log | grep Sleep` shows it). It still finishes.
- Every log line appears **twice** for launchd runs and once for manual runs. The script both writes
  to the log file and prints to stdout, and the plist captures stdout to the same file. Not a bug —
  do not "fix" it, and do not read doubled lines as two attempts.
- The script is PowerShell only because `pwsh` runs it natively. It manages launchd, not Task
  Scheduler; the Windows original is parked at `daily-backup.ps1.win-orig`.
- `-DryRun` is the only parameter. Use it to preview without writing.

## Examples

**Example 1: routine catch-up**
```
User: "run the backup"
→ Runs the script, reads backup-state.json (status OK, 0 errors)
→ "Backup done, no errors. Everything pushed and copied to Drive.
   CRASHBOX SSD wasn't plugged in, so uncommitted files were not saved.
   Plug it in and run /backup again if you have unsaved work."
```

**Example 2: session start shows a hook failure**
```
User: "the backup failed this morning — fix it"
→ Greps daily-backup.log for the error codes → DNS failure on both pushes
→ Confirms github.com reachable, re-runs the script → status OK
→ Archives and empties .errors.log so the warning stops appearing
```

definition.description:
Scrape one URL and return its content, or execute catalogued Alexandria capabilities. URL mode returns markdown by default, or HTML, links, screenshots, branding data, a targeted answer, or JSON matching a supplied schema, plus page metadata. Firecrawl may serve recently indexed content; set `maxAge: 0` for a live fetch. A successful response does not by itself confirm the page is still current. A named browser profile loads saved session data without saving changes to it.

`firecrawl_search` with `sources` unset and `firecrawl_find_tools` can discover providers for the same fields across several pages; a matching Alexandria provider returns typed records in one call.

Alexandria mode: `alexandria` selects catalogued capability execution and is mutually exclusive with `url`. Alexandria execution is billed at the capability's listed price and needs a team with Alexandria enabled.

profile.description: Loads a saved browser profile without saving changes to it.

requestId.description: Idempotency key bound to one Alexandria execution payload. Generated when omitted and returned with the result.

alexandria.description: Catalogued Alexandria capability invocation, mutually exclusive with url. One {provider, capability, options} object or an array of 1-10, with contracts available through firecrawl_search or firecrawl_find_tools. Each call may include version to pin a published workflow; omitting it uses latest. Only requestId and timeout are supported alongside alexandria. The selected contract marks required inputs and any requiresOneOf groups (at least one member per group); it may include example.request/example.response and response.key (which may differ from records). Where pagination is declared, its fields govern paging with the same filters; catalogue next is separate from provider pagination. Returns per-capability results in data.alexandria with data, records, or an error with a code; individual capabilities can fail even when the outer response succeeds. Requires an API key on a team with Alexandria enabled. Some providers require accepted terms; blocked requests return the applicable requirements.

capability.description: Capability address as returned by search or discover, e.g. "series/observations".

version.description: Optional published workflow version. Omit to use the latest version.

options.description: Capability options as declared by its contract.

definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Firecrawl__firecrawl_search
definition.description:
Search web and specialized indexes, returning ranked results with query-relevant highlights. Each web result is a title, URL, and description. Operators include quoted phrases, `-term`, `site:host`, `inurl:term`, `intitle:term`, and `related:host`; the set is non-exhaustive. `includeDomains` and `excludeDomains` are mutually exclusive hostname filters; categories limit result types to `research`, `pdf`, `developer`, or `gov`.

For a programming question, add `categories: ["developer"]`. It searches an index of public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, repository READMEs, and code documentation, and returns the results in `data.web` with `category: "developer"`.

For a legal or regulatory question, `categories: ["gov"]` returns results in `data.web` with `category: "gov"` and cannot be combined with other categories; `firecrawl_gov_search` is the dedicated tool. Verify gov results' issuer, jurisdiction, status, and version before citing current law.

Authenticated search combines web results, semantic tool summaries and domain matches. Use sources: ["alexandria"] for semantic tools only. A search with sources: ["web"] omits semantic provider discovery; domainTools: true can still return website-matched tools. Web-only results use domainTools: false. Tool matches describe available structured-data capabilities, not executed data. toolDetail: "compact" (default) returns only provider, capability and description; "summary" adds metadata; "full" includes their input and output contracts. firecrawl_scrape with an alexandria body executes a selected capability; firecrawl_find_tools provides catalogue browsing and full contracts.

Returns result groups in `data` and an operation `id`.

toolDetail.description: Compact by default. Compact returns only provider, capability and description; full includes contracts. Inspect selected compact tools with firecrawl_find_tools providers and capabilities.

query.description: Query for web and semantic tool discovery. Operators include quoted phrases, `-term`, `site:host`, `inurl:term`, `intitle:term`, and `related:host`; the set is non-exhaustive. Catalogue browsing is available through firecrawl_find_tools.

objective.description: Optional broader goal for this search, if known. Avoid sensitive information.

domainTools.description: Include domain-matched tools for result URLs. Defaults to true when Alexandria is combined with web, news or images; semantic-only search leaves domain matching off.

highlights.description: Return query-relevant page excerpts for web and news results when available (default). Highlights appear in web `description` and news `snippet`; otherwise, original snippets are returned. Set to false to keep the original search snippets.

includeDomains.description: Hostnames to restrict results to. Mutually exclusive with excludeDomains.

excludeDomains.description: Hostnames to leave out of results. Mutually exclusive with includeDomains.

sources.description: Search sources; authenticated sessions default to web + alexandria, keyless sessions to web only. A search with sources: ["web"] omits semantic provider discovery; domainTools: true can still return website-matched tools. Web-only results use domainTools: false. Use ["alexandria"] alone for provider discovery without web results.

categories.description: Limit results to specific source types. `research` restricts ordinary web results to research-affiliated websites and returns page snippets, which is separate from the `firecrawl_research_*` tools that search paper abstracts and full text across biomedical (PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv) and arXiv literature; `pdf` searches PDF results; `developer` searches an index built for coding agents over public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, repository READMEs, and code documentation; `gov` searches the Government Index of US federal, state, and local legal and regulatory sources, the index behind firecrawl_gov_search, and cannot be combined with other categories; gov hits can include historical versions, bill text, agency guidance, and third-party reproductions, so verify the issuer, jurisdiction, enacted/effective status, and version before citing current governing law, clarify a missing jurisdiction or ambiguous as-of date, and use general search for non-US questions or missing coverage (no hits does not establish that no applicable law exists). `developer` and `gov` return hits in `data.web` with `category` set to their name; the other categories also filter `data.web`.
